items.title: Switzerland Prolongs Neutrality Soul-Searching With Weapons Vote
items.author: Levin Stamm and Fabrice Obrist

items.title: Burnham’s Big Worry Isn’t Brexit or Welfare, It’s Trump and Iran
items.author: Alex Wickham
items.content: <article>In public, Andy Burnham’s recent focus has been on securing better trade terms with the European Union and reforming Britain’s welfare system. In private, the prime minister has been preoccupied by a more global problem: what happens next in the Iran war.</article>

items.title: Federal Court Halts Pregnant Workers’ Protection Law

items.title: Trump Vows To Tax US Companies Building Data Centers Abroad

On today's show, Dean Curnutt, founder and CEO of Macro Risk Advisors, says the market selloff could prove “cleansing” by resetting valuations and making room for fresh capital, but warns that the growing overlap between the AI trade and the broader economy could leave markets vulnerable to further downside. Doug Rediker, managing partner at International Capital Strategy, says the market correction is helping “rationalize and normalize” the AI thesis after a period of heavy investment and rising financing risk, calling the pullback both necessary and healthy. New Mexico Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham says prospective 2028 Democratic presidential contenders are already making their presence felt in the state, naming Mark Kelly, Rahm Emanuel, Pete Buttigieg and Cory Booker among those who have been on the ground. items.title: Historic Market Selloff Deepens After Anthropic IPO
items.content: <article>The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are ProShares Head of Research and CIO of Active Investments Alessio De Longis, PsiQuantum CEO Victor Peng, Barclays Senior Equity Analyst Brandon Oglenski, Hindlian Advisory Founder & CEO Amanda Hindlian, Charles Schwab Chief Investment Strategist Liz Ann Sonders, Envestnet CIO & EVP of Wealth Solutions Dana D’Auria, T. Rowe Price Portfolio Manager, Science & Tech Equity Tony Wang, Scribe Co-Founder & CEO Jennifer Smith, J&J Snack Foods CEO Dan Fachner, & Trujillo Group Founder Sol Trujillo & Citi Head of Wealth Andy Sieg. items.title: Gov. Lujan Grisham: 2028 Hopefuls Already Eyeing New Mexico
items.content: <article>New Mexico Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham says prospective 2028 Democratic presidential contenders are already making their presence felt in the state, naming Mark Kelly, Rahm Emanuel, Pete Buttigieg and Cory Booker among those who have been on the ground. New Mexico is set to vote fourth in the Democratic presidential primary calendar. She also discusses permitting reform and the growing data-center buildout with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Sol Trujillo Says Latino Economic Growth Is an Undervalued Investment Opportunity
items.content: <article>Sol Trujillo & Andy Sieg discuss Citi’s partnership with Trujillo to invest in and expand financial access for the Latino population in the United States. They said the opportunity is attractive but has been overlooked because investors have not segmented the data to see its scale. The two speak with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Rediker: AI Selloff Is a ‘Healthy’ Correction
items.content: <article>Doug Rediker, managing partner at International Capital Strategy, says the market correction is helping “rationalize and normalize” the AI thesis after a period of heavy investment and rising financing risk, calling the pullback both necessary and healthy. He also says geopolitical uncertainty is becoming increasingly difficult for markets to quantify, but adds that he is “not as upset as some otherwise might be” about the risks. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Stocks Plunge After Anthropic IPO, Trump Returns from Asia
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Money takes the pulse of your financial life, powered by the reporting of our global newsroom. Today's guests: Managing Partner & Head of CVC Marathon Bruce Richards and BlackRock Chief Investment & Portfolio Strategist Gargi Chaudhrui. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Curnutt: Selloff May Be ‘Cleansing,’ But Risks Remain
items.content: <article>Dean Curnutt, founder and CEO of Macro Risk Advisors, says the market selloff could prove “cleansing” by resetting valuations and making room for fresh capital, but warns that the growing overlap between the AI trade and the broader economy could leave markets vulnerable to further downside. He also sees short-dated Treasuries as a haven if the Federal Reserve is forced to reverse course. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Historic Winner of Texas Oil Regulator Seat Wants Faster Permits
items.author: David Wethe
items.content: <article>The first Democrat in 36 years to win a seat on the commission that governs the oil and gas industry in Texas said he plans to work with his Republican colleagues to speed up permitting in the state.</article>

items.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Huang Behavior Complaints
items.content:
<article>The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy.
Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF

About two decades ago, two Nvidia employees complained about how then-Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang treated his staff. Stephen Pettigrew, the first in-house lawyer hired by Nvidia, said he observed Huang regularly verbally abusing and intimidating employees, according to court documents filed in the Superior Court of California. Pettigrew alleged he was fired for raising concerns about the conduct of Nvidia executives, while the company cited performance issues for his termination, according to court documents.

On today’s episode:
Ian King, Bloomberg News US Semiconductor Reporter
Mark Gurman, Bloomberg News Managing Editor of Consumer Technology
Anna Wong, Bloomberg Economics Chief US Economist
Michael Ball, Bloomberg News Macro Strategist  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Apple Working on Own AI Agent to Rival OpenAI and Anthropic
items.content: <article>Mark Gurman, Bloomberg News managing editor of consumer technology, said that Apple is working on its own AI agent to perform tasks for consumers, acting as a consumer's 'own personal assistant' throughout their digital lives. Gurman said that there is a lot of risk for Apple because of its slow pace getting into the AI space, adding that it will be hard for consumers to undo established relationships with other AI agents like ChatGPT and Claude. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Swiss Farmers Set to Lose Voice in Government With New Minister
items.author: Bastian Benrath-Wright

items.title: Trump Threatens to Tax Firms Building Data Centers Abroad: Full Presser
items.content: <article>President Trump delivered a wide-ranging briefing to reporters after returning from his trip to Asia, where he held a landmark summit with China's President Xi and Russia's President Putin. President Trump told reporters he plans to tax on firms building data centers abroad and said that US and China are working on a 'comprehensive' deal on chips.  Trump also backed both former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, saying would like to see Huang return to the chipmaker and that he has not lost confidence in Lutnick.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>
